draft.title: The media and law reform
card: The media is the channel that carries information to the public. Traditional media includes television, radio and newspapers. Social media includes platforms where users share posts and videos.
Raising awareness
media coverage can bring a problem with the law to many people who did not know about it. Social media can spread a story quickly, and anyone can share it.
Pressure on parliament
when many people take notice of an issue, members of parliament may feel pressure to respond. This is more likely when coverage is sustained and public concern is strong.
Limits
the media does not make or change laws. Only parliament can pass a new law, and it may choose not to act.
draft.remember: The media can raise awareness and add pressure, but parliament decides whether the law changes.

a.q: Which statement best describes how the media can contribute to law reform?
opts: It informs the public and can pressure parliament to act
It passes new laws once public concern becomes strong
It forces parliament to change a law that people dislike
It investigates a law and recommends changes to parliament
a.why: The media can spread information and build public concern, which may put pressure on parliament. It cannot pass laws or force parliament to act, because only parliament makes that decision.
a.clue: Who has the power to pass a law?

b.q: A newspaper series in Victoria exposes a gap in the law, and the story spreads widely on social media. Several MPs then speak about the issue. What does this best show?
opts: Media coverage added pressure, but parliament still decides
Media coverage has changed the law through public pressure
Parliament must now pass a new law to fix the gap
Social media has replaced parliament as a source of law
b.why: The coverage raised awareness and MPs responded, which shows pressure. Speaking about an issue does not change the law, because parliament must still choose to pass a new law. The option saying the law has changed treats pressure as if it were the outcome.
b.clue: Has anything been passed by parliament yet?

a.best: It informs the public and can pressure parliament to act

b.best: Media coverage added pressure, but parliament still decides

problems.detail: 'Parliament decides whether the law changes' overstates the card's narrower 'Only parliament can pass a new law'. It conflicts with point 3, where courts can change common law directly. Something like 'parliament decides whether to pass a new law' would be accurate.
The right option is the only one with a hedge ('can pressure'), while the distractors are absolute ('passes', 'forces'). A test-wise student could pick it without knowing the idea.
